defs.d: (usually used predicatively, not attributively, be afraid) Impressed with fear or apprehension; in fear.
defs.ex: He is afraid of death.

defs.d: Regretful, sorry.
defs.ex: I am afraid I cannot help you in this matter.

defs.d: To fill with wonder and surprise; to astonish, astound, surprise or perplex.
defs.ex: He was amazed when he found that the girl was a robot.

defs.d: To undergo amazement; to be astounded.
Causing wonder and amazement; very surprising.
Possessing uniquely wonderful qualities.
To reach a partly (or totally) unqualified conclusion.
To solve by a correct conjecture; to conjecture rightly.
defs.ex: He who guesses the riddle shall have the ring.

defs.d: A set of draught animals, such as two horses in front of a carriage.
Any group of people involved in the same activity, especially sports or work.
defs.ex: The IT manager leads a team of three software developers.

defs.d: To form a group, as for sports or work.
defs.ex: They teamed to complete the project.

defs.d: (by extension) To go together well; to harmonize.
Any of various dishes commonly made by combining liquids, such as water or stock with other ingredients, such as meat and vegetables, that contribute flavor and texture.
defs.ex: Pho is a traditional Vietnamese soup.

defs.d: Any mixture or substance suggestive of soup consistency.
To feed: to provide with soup or a meal.
To develop (film) in a (chemical) developing solution.
An article of clothing that covers the part of the body between the waist and the ankles or knees, and is divided into a separate part for each leg.
defs.ex: The trousers need to be shortened.

defs.d: To give (especially public) notice of (something); to announce publicly.
To provide information about a person or goods and services to influence others.
defs.ex: For personal needs, advertise on the internet or in a local newspaper.

defs.d: A logical clause or phrase that a conditional statement uses. The phrase can either be true or false.
A requirement or requisite.
defs.ex: Environmental protection is a condition for sustainability.   What other planets might have the right conditions for life?   The union had a dispute over sick time and other conditions of employment.

defs.d: To subject to the process of acclimation.
defs.ex: I became conditioned to the absence of seasons in San Diego.

defs.d: To subject to different conditions, especially as an exercise.
defs.ex: They were conditioning their shins in their karate class.

defs.d: A grasp or grip.
defs.ex: Keep a firm hold on the handlebars.

defs.d: An act or instance of holding.
defs.ex: Can I have a hold of the baby?

defs.d: To grasp or grip.
defs.ex: Hold the pencil like this.

defs.d: To contain or store.
defs.ex: This package holds six bottles.

defs.d: A repair or corrective action.
defs.ex: That plumber's fix is much better than the first one's.

defs.d: A difficult situation; a quandary or dilemma; a predicament.
defs.ex: It rained before we repaired the roof, and were we in a fix!

defs.d: To pierce; now generally replaced by transfix.
To attach; to affix; to hold in place or at a particular time.
defs.ex: A dab of chewing gum will fix your note to the bulletin board.

defs.d: Comfortably, without discomfort or anxiety.
Without difficulty.
defs.ex: Individuals without a family network are easily controlled.

defs.d: Influenza.
Stomach flu.
For each.
defs.ex: $2.50 per dozen

defs.d: To each, in each (used in expressing ratios of units).
defs.ex: 100 centimeters per meter

defs.d: One of a pair of long flat runners designed for gliding over snow or water
One of a pair of long flat runners under some flying machines, used for landing
To move on skis
To travel over (a slope etc.) on skis; to travel on skis at (a place), (especially as a sport)
(usually capitalized) A follower of Plato, a Platonist.
A senior member of an academy, college, or university; a person who attends an academy; a person engaged in scholarly pursuits; one who is academic in practice.
Belonging to the school or philosophy of Plato
defs.ex: the academic sect or philosophy

defs.d: Belonging to an academy or other higher institution of learning; also a scholarly society or organization.
A conflagration; a flame.
A piece of burning wood or peat, or a glowing cinder.
defs.ex: To burn something to brands and ashes.

defs.d: To burn the flesh with a hot iron, either as a marker (for criminals, slaves etc.) or to cauterise a wound.
defs.ex: When they caught him, he was branded and then locked up.

defs.d: To mark (especially cattle) with a brand as proof of ownership.
defs.ex: The ranch hands had to brand every new calf by lunchtime.

defs.d: A butt or mark to shoot at, as for practice, or to test the accuracy of a firearm, or the force of a projectile.
defs.ex: Take careful aim at the target.

defs.d: A goal or objective.
defs.ex: They have a target to finish the project by November.

defs.d: To aim something, especially a weapon, at (a target).
To aim for as an audience or demographic.
defs.ex: The advertising campaign targeted older women.

defs.d: The act of complaining.
A grievance, problem, difficulty, or concern.
defs.ex: I have no complaints about the quality of his work, but I don't enjoy his company.

defs.d: Making, or tending to make, a positive impression; having power to impress
defs.ex: an impressive movie

defs.d: Capable of being impressed.
To observe or inspect carefully or critically
defs.ex: He examined the crime scene for clues.

defs.d: To check the health or condition of something or someone
defs.ex: The doctor examined the patient.

defs.d: (manner) In a fair manner; fair; not biased or skewed or favouring a certain party
defs.ex: A jury is expected to ensure that the accused is fairly judged.

defs.d: Favorably; auspiciously; commodiously.
defs.ex: a town fairly situated for foreign trade

defs.d: An aboriginal inhabitant of a region colonized by English-speaking people; in particular:
Aboriginal inhabitant of a region colonized by English-speaking people; in particular:
A person who is native to a place; a person who was born in a place.
A native speaker.
A female member of a royal family other than a queen, especially a daughter or granddaughter.
A woman or girl who excels in a given field or class.
The act of producing, making or creating something.
defs.ex: The widget making machine is being used for production now.

defs.d: The act of bringing something forward, out etc. for use or consideration.
Nervous and worried.
Having a feeling of anxiety or disquietude; extremely concerned, especially about something that will happen in the future or that is unknown.
defs.ex: I could tell she was anxious as she was biting her nails.

defs.d: A body of one or more persons convened for the accomplishment of some specific purpose, typically with formal protocols.
A guardian; someone in charge of another person deemed to be unable to look after himself or herself.
An act or episode of rescuing, saving.
A liberation, freeing.
To save from any violence, danger or evil.
defs.ex: The well-trained team rescued everyone after the avalanche.

defs.d: To free or liberate from confinement or other physical restraint.
defs.ex: to rescue a prisoner from the enemy.

defs.d: To make safe; to relieve from apprehensions of, or exposure to, danger; to guard; to protect.
To put beyond hazard of losing or of not receiving; to make certain; to assure; frequently with against or from, or formerly with of.
defs.ex: to secure a creditor against loss; to secure a debt by a mortgage

defs.d: Free from attack or danger; protected.
Free from the danger of theft; safe.
